clue.text: Sets off and reaches, in the morning, centre of Cinque Port

parts.note: to make a place is to reach it, as in 'we made it to town'
AM, ante meridiem, marks morning hours

indicators.note: only the middle of the port's name is wanted, so its first and last letters are dropped

parts.note: Dover is one of the Cinque Ports, a historic group of English Channel harbours

explanation.surface: A traveller sets off and arrives at a Kent harbour town in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cinque Ports are an old confederation of harbours in Kent and Sussex; Dover is the best known. 'centre of' trims DOVER to OVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean to start going or take action; an idiomatic equivalent of setting off.

clue.text: Club's male champion

parts.note: an ace is an expert or champion performer

explanation.surface: A sports club's star man is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club-like weapon with a spiked or flanged head, an example of a club.

clue.text: Hold the fort?

definitions.meaning: to hold something is to retain or maintain it
the strongest tower of a castle, its innermost stronghold

explanation.surface: The phrase 'hold the fort' asks someone to look after things while others are away.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb meaning retain, and a noun for the central tower of a castle, which is a fortification.

clue.text: This may be used to identify eg Neighbours tune

definitions.text: This may be used to identify

parts.note: Neighbours is a long-running Australian soap opera, an example of a serial
a number is a song or tune in a show or set

explanation.surface: Someone could recognise a TV soap from its theme tune.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is an Australian TV soap opera, long popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufacturers stamp a unique code on each item so that any single unit can be identified.

clue.text: What movement of timer may be worth

indicators.note: the letters of the clue word timer are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how valuable a clock's mechanism might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' looks like a clock's works, but it signals the rearrangement of TIMER.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns mean value or excellence that deserves recognition; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Is over par, surprisingly — electronic cigarette required

indicators.note: the letters of 'Is over par' turn up in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A golfer, over par, is reaching for a vape to calm their nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A vape device heats liquid into an inhalable mist, so an e-cigarette is one kind.

clue.text: Copied notice about gym

indicators.note: the notice wraps around the gym class, placed about it

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a public notice
PE, physical education, is school gym

explanation.surface: Someone copied an announcement concerning a gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone's behaviour is to mimic them, the verb used for monkeys copying.

clue.text: Correspondence with leader of party prior to moving on

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
the letters of 'prior to' are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Letters with a party leader before a move onward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving on' reads as one phrase, but only 'moving' is the anagram signal; 'on' stays as written at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence in the sense of agreement or balance between parts, a matching ratio.

clue.text: US lawyer staggering — judge inside gets black tea

parts.note: a DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

indicators.note: the judge goes inside the word for staggering

parts.note: reeling means staggering about unsteadily

explanation.surface: An American lawyer is reeling, and a judge drinks tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places J within REELING to give RJEELING.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian hill district gives its name to a famous fragrant black tea variety.

clue.text: Millais painting of fruit ready to be eaten

parts.note: a cherry is a small stone fruit
ripe fruit is ready for eating

explanation.surface: A Pre-Raphaelite still life of ripe fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: John Everett Millais painted 'Cherry Ripe' (1879), a portrait of a little girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a famous 1879 Victorian portrait of a child by the Pre-Raphaelite painter.

clue.text: Go round most of French city

indicators.note: most of a word is all of it except its final letter

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

explanation.surface: Visitors are urged to see most of a French city.

clue.text: Eventually storing weapons some distance away

parts.note: at length means eventually, after a long time
arms are weapons

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something at a limb's reach means holding it away from yourself, at a distance.

clue.text: Achievement demonstrating skill of expert oarsman

parts.note: a master is an expert
the stroke is the rower who sets the pace in a crew

explanation.surface: A skilled rower's feat is praised.
explanation.walkthrough: In a rowing eight, the stroke sits nearest the stern and sets the rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: A brilliant, decisive move is a coup of great ingenuity, exactly a skilled achievement.

clue.text: Grass-covered ground? Environmentalists' department

parts.note: Greens are environmentalist campaigners or party members
a ward is an administrative division, as of a city or hospital

explanation.surface: A green-party department claiming ownership of a lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Sward is turf, and a literary word for a stretch of lawn or grassy land.

clue.text: Envoys, English, fail to see sign

clue.text: Hints about bodyguards

parts.note: RE means about or concerning
minders are bodyguards, people who look after someone

explanation.surface: Tips on hiring personal protection.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompts that jog the memory are gentle hints, nudges to recall something.

clue.text: Outgoing type, former scout, entering IOM races

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the scout goes in between the letters of the races

parts.note: the TT (Tourist Trophy) motorcycle races are held on the Isle of Man
a Rover was a senior member of the Scout movement

explanation.walkthrough: IOM is the Isle of Man, home of the TT motorbike races; Rover Scouts were the senior Scout section.
explanation.definitionFit: A sociable, gregarious person is described as outgoing, the psychological opposite of an introvert.

clue.text: Carnivore later let loose

indicators.note: the letters of 'later' are freed to form a new order

explanation.surface: A meat-eating animal will be released at a later date.

clue.text: Racecourse out of step, so modernising

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in 'step, so modernising'

explanation.surface: A racecourse is behind the times and is updating itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Surrey course is home to the Derby, one of Britain's best-known horse racing venues.

clue.text: Spurns county on occasions

parts.note: turns are occasions or goes, as in 'taking turns'

explanation.surface: A county is repeatedly rejected.

clue.text: Ray, pupil staying at a school, is one who has fun riding on wheels?

definitions.text: one who has fun riding on wheels?

parts.note: a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish
a boarder is a pupil who lives at the school

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a boy's name but is the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider on a four-wheeled board, rolling and doing tricks for fun, fits the playful description.

clue.text: Jar I smashed containing last of prosecco wine

the jar and I are broken up into a new arrangement

clue.text: Spades on top of pile in game

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
nap is the raised pile on fabric

explanation.definitionFit: A children's card game where players shout on spotting matching cards; one example of a game.

clue.text: Agent following current game

clue.text: Ruin aerial

a concave antenna for receiving satellite signals

clue.text: Dance waving pretty sash
